title: [GOOD] Proper hop_limit clamping prevents flood amplification attacks
description:
File: rust/lichen-core/src/loadng.rs
Lines: 345-348, 689-726

What's good: RREQ parsing clamps hop_limit to MAX_HOP_LIMIT (15) to prevent flood amplification attacks where an attacker sends RREQ with hop_limit=255 to cause excessive network-wide propagation.

The implementation includes:
1. Clear SECURITY comment explaining the threat model
2. Test coverage for boundary values (255, 15, 4)
3. Consistent handling with expanding ring limits [4, 8, 15]

Worth defending: The asymmetry between parse (clamp) and serialize (raw) could be seen as inconsistent, but clamping on parse is the right choice - untrusted input is the threat, not local serialization.
close_reason: Acknowledged: Positive observation about proper hop_limit clamping via EXPANDING_RING constants.
